I just noticed that we might not have marked the Beacon root precompile as a warm precompile - is this part of devnet8 spec (beacon root precompile should be warm?) ( <@792822129019584562> ) I think on top of 2929 it should be warm, but I am rather sure it is not warm for us, which is weird because we pass pyspec tests? most likely our canonical number to block mapping for that block is messedup as the top (and rest of chain matches) also for lodeatar<>ethereumjs pair even that is matching, so its not state related lodestar<>ethereumjs was re-synced from wiped db i i don't think any txs using precompiles have yet been seeded , <@412614104222531604> let know if you know better It should be a tx not directly calling into the precompile So via a contract, otherwise the warm/cold check is not done I am rather sure such Tx will break us (or via create tx) `5F5F60205F5F600B5AF1` this payload should do it Hm nvm you need an actual timestamp so you dont consume all gas at the precompile... maybe it still breaks though not sure we can send a payload and confirm which clients break alongside us and deploy the fix but this block hash differing is separate issue, most likely with our canonical num => block mapping staying unchanged because of some edge condition, will look into it I think you mean that our number => hash for the canonical chain is not up-to-date with the actual canonical chain right? for that block because there might be some forking there Yes exactly we have had such issues in past though i thought i fixed it, may be some edge case still remains I don't think any of the pyspec tests use a default warm for the beacon root predeploy, except for the tests where we add the address and storage keys to the tx access lists, but otherwise it should always be cold (at least last time I checked the spec) We match this spec. However, I don't think it matches the current beacon precompile spec if you also read EIP 2929, since beacon precompile is a precompile, it should technically be warm..? But technically it's not a precompile, it's a predeployed contract
